key_insight: Adding zero-knowledge proofs to quantum oblivious transfer can reduce required quantum communication by 10–100× at a fixed security target.
engineering_relevance: The approach could ease quantum communication requirements and tolerate noisier channels, but shifts substantial cost to classical computation.
method: Require the receiver to prove honest execution of crucial protocol steps without revealing extra information.
Use these proofs to tighten security bounds against malicious receivers.
Introduce a tunable variant that trades computational overhead for communication savings.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parameter-dependent communication reductions of one to two orders of magnitude and an increase in maximum tolerable channel error rate from approximately 3.5% to 9%.
watch_item: Estimated proof-computation overhead substantially exceeds quantum acquisition time, potentially outweighing communication savings.
paper_title: Improving Quantum Oblivious Transfer using Zero-Knowledge Proofs
